section_summary: This section consists mainly of State Department and FBI correspondence about suspected Japanese espionage, couriers, propaganda, businesses, and diplomatic activity in Argentina during 1945. Several reports investigate particular people or firms but say that surveillance did not establish current subversive activity. The section also includes an embassy note concerning Japanese social organizations and an apparently unrelated routing note.

subfiles.title: Airgram on Japanese diplomatic activities in Argentina
subfiles.about: Reports the freedom and continued influence of Japanese diplomats in Argentina after the break in relations.
subfiles.summary: The embassy describes Japanese diplomats as directing community organizations and potentially espionage while retaining diplomatic privileges. It recounts meetings, nationalist ceremonies, and confidential reports of speeches to Japanese groups.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal on Delgado, Márquez, and Muñoz
subfiles.about: Forwards an inquiry into three people alleged to have undertaken subversive activity.
subfiles.summary: Forwards a confidential report on alleged espionage by three theatrical-company members.

subfiles.title: Report on the Piquer theatrical company
subfiles.about: Investigates alleged espionage by members of a Spanish theatrical company in Buenos Aires.
subfiles.summary: Surveillance recorded ordinary social activity by Delgado and other company members. Sources discussed the company and its star, Conchita Piquer, but the report gives no clear evidence of espionage.

subfiles.title: FBI letter on Hidenosuke Ueda
subfiles.about: Reports Ueda's past association with Goro Miyasaki and probable presence near Córdoba.
subfiles.summary: Distinguishes Hidenosuke Ueda from Heisaku Ueda, who had been detained by Argentine police.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal on Nobuo Yatoh and Mahoichi Hiramatsu
subfiles.about: Forwards a memorandum concerning Yatoh's correspondence with Hiramatsu.
subfiles.summary: Notes political and economic information in Yatoh's letters and Hiramatsu's current Buenos Aires connections.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Nobuo Yatoh and Mahoichi Hiramatsu
subfiles.about: Traces Hiramatsu's residence, business connections, correspondence, and names in Yatoh's address books.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum reviews Yatoh's suspected intelligence work and Hiramatsu's links to Japanese trading firms and community organizations. It follows intercepted correspondence with Bolivia and inquiries into several address-book entries, without establishing the significance of every contact.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal on the Tomiya Koseki case
subfiles.about: Forwards a summary of clandestine Japanese correspondence between Chile and Argentina.
subfiles.summary: Identifies Koseki, couriers, intermediaries, and the types of information sought by Japanese agents.

subfiles.title: Summary memorandum on Tomiya Koseki and clandestine correspondence
subfiles.about: Details a Japanese correspondence network linking the embassy in Buenos Aires with contacts in Chile.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum describes couriers, coded letters concealed in envelopes, and U.S. embassy stationery sent from Santiago to Buenos Aires. It identifies Shōzō Murai as the operational contact under Koseki and discusses arrests of Carlos Santa Cruz and associates. Later pages provide biographies, addresses, contacts, and suspected roles for the Chilean and Japanese participants.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal on Mitsui and Nambei Trading Company
subfiles.about: Forwards an investigation of a Buenos Aires branch of Mitsui and its managers.
subfiles.summary: Describes surveillance of Nambei manager Isoma Kobayashi and a visit to a private residence.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Nambei Trading Company personnel
subfiles.about: Investigates Nambei personnel, their contacts, premises, and travel.
subfiles.summary: Surveillance follows Kobayashi and other people connected with Nambei Trading Company. The report examines residences, vehicles, visitors, and travel within Argentina, while much of the OCR on these pages is illegible.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal on Toshiyuki Shibata
subfiles.about: Forwards findings on Shibata, previously suspected of collecting shipping information.
subfiles.summary: Reports quiet domestic activity and no confirmed Japanese embassy connection.

subfiles.title: Report on Toshiyuki Shibata
subfiles.about: Reviews surveillance and earlier allegations involving Shibata.
subfiles.summary: Records earlier trade and shipping material, but says recent observation found no suspicious activity.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal on Japanese activities in Argentina
subfiles.about: Forwards a confidential report on Japanese activities in Buenos Aires.
subfiles.summary: Sends an investigative memorandum also available to the U.S. embassies in Santiago and Buenos Aires.

subfiles.title: Report on Mutsuo Watanabe and Gintaro Tani
subfiles.about: Examines former Japanese embassy clerks who received overseas correspondence and maintained embassy contacts.
subfiles.summary: The report traces Watanabe's addresses, mail from Chile and other countries, and visits by former embassy officials. It describes Tani's contacts, an unidentified Argentine visitor, internment at La Falda, and plans for further inquiry. Its final page lists investigative leads and sources.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal on Yuichi Takeuchi
subfiles.about: Forwards a memorandum on the activities of Yuichi Takeuchi in Buenos Aires.
subfiles.summary: Sends confidential findings about the Japanese trading representative.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Yuichi Takeuchi and Okura & Company
subfiles.about: Investigates allegations that Takeuchi used Okura offices and contacts for espionage.
subfiles.summary: The report reviews suspected mail aliases, Japanese visitors, a German acquaintance, and Okura's former offices. Surveillance found Takeuchi largely inactive, although Okura retained a mail box and he collected its correspondence.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal on Kingo Kawai
subfiles.about: Forwards information concerning Kingo Kawai's activities in Buenos Aires.
subfiles.summary: Introduces a confidential memorandum about suspected Japanese espionage linked to a fishing company.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Kingo Kawai and the CACIP fishing company
subfiles.about: Examines suspected espionage involving Japanese-owned fishing trawlers and Kingo Kawai.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum describes CACIP's ownership, directors, vessels, offices, and Argentine government intervention. It recounts allegations about shipboard activity but says surveillance of Kawai's home and trips to the company office found nothing unusual.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal on suspected Japanese espionage
subfiles.about: Forwards confidential information on suspected Japanese espionage in Argentina.
subfiles.summary: Introduces an attached memorandum on several Japanese subjects.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Daizaburo Suematsu and associates
subfiles.about: Investigates Suematsu, associates, embassy contacts, and possible shipping intelligence.
subfiles.summary: The report reviews earlier suspicions and follows Suematsu's residence, visitors, and association with Mario Campiglio. It records contacts and correspondence but provides no clear demonstration of current espionage.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal on Angel A. Perrone
subfiles.about: Forwards surveillance findings on a correspondent suspected of relaying intelligence to Madrid.
subfiles.summary: Reports no definite subversive activity and a possible switch from cables to airmail.

subfiles.title: Report on Angel A. Perrone
subfiles.about: Describes Perrone's movements, employment, communications, and press interests.
subfiles.summary: Surveillance follows Perrone between home and an Interior Ministry office and records his interest in a newspaper account of Japanese treatment of Australian prisoners. Investigators reviewed possible reports to Madrid but observed no definite subversive conduct.

subfiles.title: Routing note on a constitution and presidential election
subfiles.about: Relays Pancho Arias's comments on constitutional approval and a presidential election.
subfiles.summary: Arias predicts elections in 1946 and denies friction with President Jiménez.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal on Julio Guido Amuchástegui
subfiles.about: Forwards an investigation of allegations that Amuchástegui aided Japanese espionage or propaganda.
subfiles.summary: Reports his advertising employment and no established suspicious activity.

subfiles.title: Report on Julio Guido Amuchástegui
subfiles.about: Reviews Amuchástegui's employment, contacts, finances, and surveillance.
subfiles.summary: Sources describe his advertising work and drinking; surveillance found contacts apparently tied to business or ordinary social activity.

subfiles.title: Embassy despatch on Japanese social organizations
subfiles.from: John M. Cabot, U.S. Embassy, Buenos Aires
subfiles.about: Transmits a note verbale asking Argentina to investigate Japanese social organizations.
subfiles.summary: Cabot reports that Foreign Minister Cooke promised to refer the matter to the proper authorities.

subfiles.title: Note verbale on Japanese social organizations
subfiles.to: Argentine Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Worship
subfiles.about: Requests inquiry into Japanese organizations considered possible centers of Axis influence.
subfiles.summary: Invokes an inter-American resolution and refers to an attached list of organizations.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal on Albino Pugnalin
subfiles.about: Forwards a report on wartime allegations of Japanese espionage by Pugnalin.
subfiles.summary: Reports no subversive activity observed in June 1945.

subfiles.title: Report on Albino Pugnalin and Antonio Agritos
subfiles.about: Investigates alleged Japanese espionage contacts and propaganda linked to Pugnalin.
subfiles.summary: The report reviews allegations involving Pugnalin, a seaman named Agritos, Japanese newspapers, and a printing shop. Surveillance found no espionage activity, and inquiry did not confirm a Foreign Ministry post or newspaper production at the suspected shop.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal on Osaka Shosen Kabushiki Kaisha
subfiles.about: Forwards an investigation of a shipping line alleged to be a Japanese espionage center.
subfiles.summary: Notes meetings at its office and British publications delivered for employee Maria Ramos.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Osaka Shosen Kabushiki Kaisha
subfiles.about: Investigates the shipping line's offices, visitors, employees, and alleged espionage role.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum follows activity at the Buenos Aires shipping office, including meetings, removal of furnishings and bundles, and individual visitors. It checks addresses and employment details for people associated with the company. Much of the OCR in this document is incomplete.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal on Masao Tsuda
subfiles.about: Forwards an inquiry into the current activities of former Japanese agent Masao Tsuda.
subfiles.summary: Reports that Tsuda remained free and that no current pro-Japanese activity was established.

subfiles.title: Report on Masao Tsuda and related inquiries
subfiles.about: Reviews Tsuda's past intelligence activity and his circumstances after release from jail.
subfiles.summary: The report describes Tsuda's residence, possessions, and conversations about the war; investigators found no current subversive activity. Its later pages turn to Paul Fernández de la Puente and possible Japanese contacts. Page 73 contains no readable OCR text.
